correctness.rationale: For each t>0 the transient Green function exists and is nonnegative. A common-source rate group changes exactly one row of M, so all G entries equal nonnegative-affine numerator divided by a positive nonnegative-affine determinant. Log derivatives of positive entries lie in [-1,1]. The raw mth moment is a strictly positive finite sum of products of m such entries, giving [-m,m]; time scaling yields edge sum -m; one-step exponential and two-state recurrent excursion networks attain the negative and limiting positive extremes. Full state-clock scaling makes U_m a finite positive exponential polynomial, yielding gradient -mean counts and Hessian their covariance. Checks passed: six exact symbolic sharpness orders, 864 group-derivative checks, 864 finite-change checks, 576 Hessian checks on 144 networks. Finite checks corroborate rather than establish general proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly identifies higher-moment local sensitivity as a natural hard extension. Rare-long completion excursions affect high raw moments; sharp m-order response bounds answer how strongly one rate/source group can perturb their magnitude independently of kinetic architecture. The covariance Hessian supplies a global convex map for multi-state clock tuning, with an exact sensitivity budget. Explicit +/-m examples show a substantive sharp boundary, not an arbitrary numerical slice or restatement of a known table.
